label: text
text: Mr. John James Withers, Conservative, has been returned unopposed to the House of Commons for Cambridge University in succession to the late Rt. Horn J. P. Rawlinson who had been Unionist Ml. P. since 1906.

label: text
text: [Mr. J. J. Withers, G.B.E., 10-18, Fellow of St. Catherine's College, Cambridge, 1920; solicitor, senior partner, in firm of Wishers Bensons, Currie, Williams & Co., was born on December 21, 1863, being a son of Mr. James Tuck, Withers. He was educated at Eton and King's College, Cambridge. He was married in 1893 to Caroline Gifford, daughter of Dr. Gifford Ramsford. He has for many years been a co-opted member of the Cambridge University Appointments Board, a Director of the Legal and General Assurance Society Limited; and Hon. Secretary of the Alpine Club, 1909-11. During the war he assisted the Propaganda Department and Ministry of Information Publications. He has published the Register of King's College, Cambridge (1903), various sections of the Alpine Club Edition of Ball's Central's Alps, and various articles on mountaineering in Alpine Journal. His recreations are mountaineering and rowing.

label: paragraph_title
text:
FULILE EFFORTS TO END
WIRELESS STRIKE

label: text
text: The protracted negotiations between the representatives of the marine wireless operators on strike and the ship owners have ended in a deadlock with no immediate, prospect of settlement according to the Chairman of the Operators' Association, who said that the employers simply repeated their terms and gave the Association seven days to accept, threatening, in the event of refusal, to offer certain conditions to the men individually.

label: text
text: The failure to agree was confirmed to the questions of wages and reinstatement of the strikers, the employers insisting that the men resume at reduced rates and be reinstated only as the employers are able to offer them service.

label: text
text: The Chairman concluded that 1,300 ships are now going to sea without qualified wireless operators, of whom over 1,900 are on strike.

label: text
text: The Wireless Telegraphists Association, in a statement, says that the operators are prepared to submit the whole dispute to the Industrial Court, but they are not prepared to prejudice the case before the Court by accepting a totally unjustified reduction.

label: text
text: It points out that the wireless operators accepted reductions in 1922 and 1924 additional to any reduction accepted by other sea-faring men.

label: text
text:
FOR FAILURE TO SETTLE
SOVIET QUARREL.

label: text
text: The Russo-Swiss reconciliation on which depends the Soviets' participation in the League's armament Conference, is making little headway, judging from the official statement from Moscow blaming the Swiss attitude for the failure to settle the dispute through the medium of France, declaring that Switzerland insisted on eliminating from the text of its declaration anything that could be interpreted as an unqualified expression of regret for the assassination of Vorovsky and refused to consent to any formula establishing an agreement to compensate Vorovsky's daughter.

label: text
text: The Soviet statement, however, ratefully, acknowledges the efforts of the French Government.

label: text
text: M. Chicherin's reply to the League's invitation to participate in the preparatory meeting of the Disarmament Conference says that the Soviet cannot attend any conference on Swiss territory pending a settlement of its conflict with Switzerland. It hopes that the obstacles will be eliminated, otherwise, the Soviet will hold the Council of the League responsible for its exclusion.

label: text
text: The newspapers congratulate Mr. Briand. Premier, on forcing the issue in last night's debate and emphasise that thereby a new majority has, appeared from which the Sociakists are excluded. The way has been opened for urgent solutions, though the "Figuro" is of opinion that the Government's troubles are about to begin, and the main difficulty will be to persuade the Chamber to give a positive vote on the fresh taxation clauses and then to secure a working majority.

label: text
text: "La Venir" similarly thinks that whilst the vote demonstrated that the Cartel is inoperable; it has not strengthened the Government. The "Matin" declares that as the three main clauses in the Cartel's financial scheme was rejected the whole scheme may be regarded as washed out

label: text
text: After the uncomfortable experience of being split in three by the debate on the vote of confidence in the Government, the Radical-Socialist group has called a Congress aiming at renewed unity, preferably avoiding a Ministerial crisis.

Importance is attached by one. Press to a meeting of mine owners which will be held this week to consider the coal situation.
It is stated that on both sides during recent weeks a growing feeling has been displayed in favour of making a further attempt to secure a peaceful solution of the problem.

label: text
text: Meanwhile, the members of the Coal Commission, in order that the Prime Minister shall have a report at the end of the month, have been working about thirteen hours a day for the past fortnight.

text: LATVIA TURNS TABLES ON THE SOVIET.

label: text
text:
There has been a development of the 'Russd/Latvian incident.'
The Latvians have sent a Note to the Soviet demanding a thorough investigation into the frontier incident, which occurred on February 12 when five men crossed the frontier and, it is alleged, assaulted and carried off a policeman. The Note demands the repatriation of the policeman and the punishment of the ctil prits.

label: text
text: The Foreign Ministry announces that a provisional Fured-Dutch Trade Agreement has been concluded, and will come into force on Monday for six months, whereby both countries will enjoy most favoured nation treatment. Negotiations for a permanent agreement have already begun.

label: text
text: The Soviet debt delegation has arrived here. It will be headed by the Soviet Ambassador, M. Rakovsky.

text:
The rainfall for January at the Botanical Gardens was 31 inch on 4 days; at the Matilda Hospital, it was 35 inch on 3 days; and at the Taipo Police Station, it was a blank both in inches and days.
The lowest reading of the barometer (means a level) was 29.927 inches at 3 p.m. on the 18th.
The maximum squall velocity, as recorded by the Dines-Baxtendell anemograph, was at the rate of 44 miles per hour at 6.19 a.m. on the 3rd.

label: text
text:
The mean temperature for the month was 61.1 degrees. The highest was 75.6 on the 18th and the lowest 51.5 on the 22nd.
There were 172.9 hours of sunshine during the month.
The Observatory recorded a total rainfall of.215 inch.

label: text
text: An old Jew lay a-dying. He was sinking fast and his sight was failing him. In feeble tones he spoke to his family gathered round the bedside. "Is Rachael there?" he asked. "Yes, dear, I'm here," replied his wife.

label: text
text:
"Yes, father."
"Is Hymn thers?"
"Yes, father."
"Is little Abie there?"
"Yes, father."
"Is my daughter Leah there?"
"Yes, father."
"Are you all there, every one of you?"
"Yes, father," came the chorus.
"Then who's looking after the shop?"

text: The football match was very exciting. Over 6,000 people were present. The ground at the start was hard and dry, but there was a drizzle in the first half and a downpour all through the second half. This quickly rendered conditions unpleasant.

text: Shanghai equalised five minutes later by a penalty taken by Goldman.

Cannes Feb. 13.
Mile. Lenglen has summoned pressmen and photographers to Carlton courts and made a statement that she was not connected with the agitation for barring photographers and cinematographers from the courts. She desired all photographers to be allowed to enter and if there was any further bother on the matter she would feel inclined to withdraw from the tournament.
At a meeting of pressmen, photographers and cinematographers at the Carlton Hotel in the evening, Mr. F. M. B. Fisher, presiding announced that rights of filming the match were now open to purchase the original option having been returned.

label: text
text:
At a stormy meeting of pressmen and cinematographers at the Carlton Hotel Cannes, presided over by Mr. F. M. B. Fisher, it was announced that no bids had been received for the exclusive cinema rights of the Lenglen. v. Wills match, and that the management of the Carlton Club were prepared to allow cinematographers to enter on a payment of £25 each.
The cinematographers, however, flatly refused to pay.

label: text
text: After a long discussion, the management yielded and consequently cinematographers will be allowed free entry to the match on Tuesday.
